entries.message: <{tag}> binds `.{name}`, which replaces the element's content, and also has content of its own — markup or a child binding, which the write would strand.
entries.fix: Bind one or the other: the property alone (`<{tag} .{name}=${…}></{tag}>`), or the content alone.

entries.message: received a bound property `.{key}` (or `!{key}`), but its class declares `{key}` as a getter with no setter — the value cannot be delivered and the binding is ignored.
entries.fix: Add a setter, or stop binding it.

entries.message: `{name}` controls only ONE selection here, and a selection the user adds is kept — it is not controlled.
entries.fix: Bind `?selected=${…}` on each <option> to control every selection.

entries.message: an expression in tag position (`<${…}>`) cannot be a tag name — a tag name must be a tag value.

the value bound by `.{name}=${…}` was replaced while the element upgraded. A class field is the usual cause: at ES2022 `{name}?: …` emits `{name};`, which runs during upgrade and overwrites whatever was set beforehand.
entries.fix: Write it `declare {name}?: …` instead. A component that calls init() adopts bound properties automatically and never sees this; this element did not. Ignore this if the component replaced the value on purpose.
